compiled_state.description:
## Observation

`make verify` on worktree fix-manta (commit de8fb7c4a8a, 2026-11-03, started ~17:52 PST, 4 h 36 min wall at host load 33-47 on 18 cores) reported `tests/unit/test_opcert_key_copy_leak_tortoise.py::test_signer_test_modules_leave_no_key_copy_in_the_temp_dir` as FAILED with `worker 'gw3' crashed` / `rebar crash guard: xdist worker=gw3 terminated abnormally: Not properly terminated`. No traceback and no pytest-timeout `Timeout` marker reached the log.

- At 18:30 PST `ps` showed the test running on an xdist worker.
- Rerun alone on the same commit at load ~40: passed, 116.44 s call time.
- The repo sets pytest-timeout `timeout = 300` with `timeout_method = "thread"`; a thread-method expiry ends the worker with `os._exit`, which xdist reports as a crash.
- The test runs a nested pytest over `test_opcert_service.py` and `test_opcert_service_integrity.py`.

Related, closed: `deformed-cherubical-flycatcher` (nested tortoise run exceeded the 300 s budget).

## Hypotheses (unproven)

1. The nested run exceeded the 300 s per-test timeout under host load, and the thread-method kill surfaced as a worker crash.
2. The worker died for another reason (memory pressure, an external signal) while the nested run was in flight.

## Next check

Run the test under a 4-worker xdist session with an induced CPU load and `-o timeout=...` lowered toward the measured call time, and check whether the outcome is the same "worker crashed" result; separately record the nested run's wall time inside the test.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The cause of the worker crash is identified with a reproduction.
- [ ] The test reports its failure as an ordinary assertion or timeout failure naming the nested run's duration, not as a bare worker crash, or its runtime is reduced so it fits its budget under the CI-equivalent load.
compiled_state.title: Opcert key-copy tortoise test crashes its xdist worker during a loaded make verify
